title: Premier Cloud SOW Intake
description: Structured inputs required to generate a Premier Cloud Statement of Work. Every field carries an `x-question` (what to ask in the meeting) and an `x-source` (where the answer normally comes from). The validator uses `x-question` to build the gap report.

sow_type.description: Selects the template. gemini_enterprise_implementation = seat-based GE rollout with connectors (CoachHub, City Winery). agent_pilot = fixed-term pilot proving one or more agents against named use cases (Afni GECX). workspace_migration = M365/other -> Google Workspace data + identity migration (Miles Partnership).
sow_type.x-question: Is this a Gemini Enterprise rollout, an agent/CX pilot, or a Workspace migration?
sow_type.x-source: Opportunity type in CRM; obvious from the meeting.

title.x-source: Deal name. e.g. 'Gemini Enterprise Implementation SOW'.

subtitle.x-source: e.g. 'Gemini Enterprise for CX Voice Agent Pilots - IT Service Desk, Progressive CCC & FNOL'.

date.x-question: What date goes on the cover?

legal_name.x-question: What is the customer's exact legal entity name?
legal_name.x-source: MSA / order form. NOT the brand name - 'Afni, Inc.' not 'Afni'.

short_name.x-question: What short name should the body text use?

address.x-source: Order form or the POC's signature block.

industry.x-source: Used in the Customer Profile paragraph.

employee_count.x-source: Used in profile narrative for pilot and migration SOWs.

profile.x-question: One paragraph: who is this customer and what do they do?
profile.x-source: Required for agent_pilot and workspace_migration; omitted in the GE implementation template.

contact.description: The named SOW point of contact in section 1.

name.x-question: Who is the customer's SOW point of contact?

signatory.description: Who actually signs. Defaults to `customer.contact` when absent.

name.x-question: Who signs on the customer side?
name.x-source: Often the CIO/CTO, not the day-to-day contact.

stakeholders.description: Named people with a role in delivery. Feeds section 9/10 Customer Team Roles.
stakeholders.x-question: Who on the customer side owns which part of delivery?
stakeholders.x-source: Attendee list + who spoke to what in the meeting.

partner.description: Premier Cloud side. Almost always inherited from library/defaults.json - only override when the deal team differs.

profile.x-source: library/defaults.json holds the standard boilerplate; override only to re-angle it for the vertical.

contact.x-question: Which Premier Cloud person is the SOW point of contact?

signatory.x-source: Historically Lee Henwood or Jason Murray-Rosel.

msa_style.description: public_link = the standard 'available at premiercloud.com/...' preamble. dated_mpsa = 'pursuant to the Master Professional Services Agreement dated <date>' (used when a negotiated MSA exists).
msa_style.x-question: Is there a signed MSA with this customer, or do we point at the public one?

msa_date.x-question: What is the date of the executed MSA?

execution_date.description: Date string or the literal 'date of last signature'.
execution_date.x-question: What is the SOW execution date?
execution_date.x-source: Target signature date agreed in the meeting.

effective_date.x-source: Explicit in the meeting, or execution date + N business days.

end_date.x-question: What is the estimated end date?

duration_weeks.x-question: How many weeks is the engagement?
duration_weeks.x-source: 5 weeks for a standard GE implementation, 8 for a pilot, 10 for a migration.

extendable_note.description: Adds the 'may be extended upon mutual written agreement' sentence.

background.description: Section 3. The narrative heart of the SOW and the part most directly mined from meeting notes.

product_intro.x-source: library/defaults.json ships the standard Gemini Enterprise paragraph.

business_challenges.x-question: What business problems is the customer trying to solve? Any numbers behind them?
business_challenges.x-source: The pain the customer described in discovery. Quantify wherever they gave you a number - ticket volumes, handle time, hours lost.

objective.x-question: In one paragraph, what is this engagement meant to prove or deliver?

key_focus_areas.x-question: What are the three or four headline workstreams?

engagement_type.x-question: Is this an execution engagement or an advisory one, and what does that mean for who does the work?

baseline_metrics.x-question: What is today's baseline we will measure against?
baseline_metrics.x-source: Numbers the customer quoted. Always record where the number came from.

platform.description: Gemini Enterprise specifics. Required for sow_type = gemini_enterprise_implementation.

seats.x-question: How many Gemini Enterprise seats are being provisioned?
seats.x-source: Order form. Drives the user-community cap and the success criteria.

identity_provider.x-source: Google Identity, Entra ID, Okta. Anything other than Google Identity changes the assumptions and adds an Identity Architect.

workforce_identity_federation.x-question: Is Workforce Identity Federation in play, and who sets it up?
workforce_identity_federation.x-source: Determines which assumption paragraph is used and whether WIF lands in Out of Scope.

environment.x-question: Are we deploying into a production or non-production project?

user_community.x-question: Which teams or departments are the in-scope users?

data_sources.x-question: Exactly which data sources get connected?
data_sources.x-source: Name every one. Connector count drives price, timeline and the success criteria line.

cloud_foundations.x-question: Does the customer already have a Google Cloud org, or do we stand up foundations?
cloud_foundations.x-source: If they have no GCP org, set true - this injects the Identity & Access Configuration and Resource Implementation scope blocks.

agentic_workflows.x-question: Are we building any no-code agents, and what does each do?
agentic_workflows.x-source: If empty, 'Developing agentic workflows' is added to Out of Scope automatically.

activation_plan.description: Google increasingly requires this. Include whenever the deal is PSF-funded against a licence commitment.
activation_plan.x-question: What activation numbers are we committing to at project end and end + 4 weeks?

golden_dataset.description: Whether the customer provides sample Q&A pairs for evaluation.

use_cases.description: Required for sow_type = agent_pilot. Each renders a full subsection with Current Solution / Proposed Solution.

name.x-question: What is each use case called?

summary.description: One-line entry in the use-case list at the top of the section.

current_solution.x-question: How does this workflow run today, step by step?
current_solution.x-source: Walk the customer through it in discovery and number the steps. This is the single most meeting-dependent field in the document.

proposed_solution.x-question: What will we build, and how does it change that flow?

systems.x-question: Which systems of record does it read from and write back to?

trigger.x-question: What triggers it - inbound call, API, work basket?

success_metrics.x-question: How will we know this use case worked?

figures.description: Figure captions; diagrams are pasted in manually after generation.

price.description: Per-use-case line item in the compensation table.

destination_platform.default: Google Workspace (Gmail, Drive, Shared Drives, Calendar)

mailbox_count.x-question: How many mailboxes, and what is the size distribution?
mailbox_count.x-source: The size distribution drives the wave plan - ask for a breakdown, not just a total.

volumes.x-question: How much data per system - mail, OneDrive, SharePoint, PSTs?
volumes.x-source: Total TB drives worker-pool sizing and the timeline.

in_scope.x-question: Which endpoint platforms are actually in scope?

endpoints.x-question: How many domain-joined devices, on what platforms, managed by what?

sso_apps.x-question: Which applications authenticate through AD today and need re-pointing to Google?
sso_apps.x-source: Get the actual list, not a count - each one needs a validation line.

worker_nodes.x-question: How many CloudM workers, split how?

tracks.description: Parallel workstreams. Each track has ordered phases; each phase has bullets.
tracks.x-question: What are the parallel tracks and their phase-by-phase plan?

plan_link.x-question: Is there a live project plan / Gantt sheet to link?

decisions_pending.x-question: What customer decisions are still open, and by when are they needed?
decisions_pending.x-source: These become dated dependencies. Every open decision in the notes belongs here.

summary_blocks.description: Summary of Scope subsections. Defaults per sow_type from library/defaults.json.

service_sections.description: Section 5 'Description of Services'. Defaults per sow_type, then customised.

out_of_scope_extra.x-question: What did the customer ask about that we are explicitly NOT doing?
out_of_scope_extra.x-source: Everything raised in the meeting and parked. The standard exclusion list is applied automatically - this adds the deal-specific ones, which are the ones that prevent scope disputes.

out_of_scope_suppress.description: Substrings of standard exclusions to drop, for when the deal actually includes them.

weeks.x-question: How many weeks does the Gantt cover?

milestones.x-question: What are the milestones and which week does each land in?

schedule.description: Optional dated task schedule (agent_pilot) or effort schedule (workspace_migration).
schedule.x-question: What is the dated task-by-task schedule, with effort where we quote hours?

deliverables.x-question: What artefacts does the customer physically receive, and when?
deliverables.x-source: Must reconcile 1:1 with the milestones. Defaults exist per sow_type.

resources.description: Resource Allocation table (workspace_migration). Include only when quoting hours.
resources.x-question: Who is staffed, for how many hours, doing what?

risks.x-question: What could derail this, specific to this customer?
risks.x-source: Five standard risks are applied automatically. Add the deal-specific ones you heard - unconfirmed API access, stakeholder turnover, resource constraints.

assumptions.x-question: What are we assuming that, if wrong, changes price or timeline?

prerequisites_before.x-question: What must the customer have done BEFORE we start?

prerequisites_ongoing.x-question: What must the customer keep doing DURING the engagement?

success_criteria.x-question: What does done look like, in terms we can hold up at closure?

total_fixed_price.x-question: What is the total fixed price?

line_items.x-question: How does the price break down?

google_funding.x-question: How much Google funding, and is it approved?
google_funding.x-source: PSF amount. Always rendered as a negative credit line.

funding_stage.x-question: What opportunity stage is the funding request at?

funding_clawback.x-question: Does the customer get invoiced the full fee if funding is not approved?
funding_clawback.x-source: TRUE when the customer pays a net amount (Miles). The clawback paragraph is a material commercial term - never omit it when net > 0.

google_data_sharing_consent.description: Adds the Google usage-data consent paragraph and third-party-beneficiary clause.

provenance.description: Written by the extraction step. Keeps the SOW auditable back to the meeting.

sources.description: Doc IDs / file names / meeting dates the intake was built from.

assumed.description: Values the model inferred rather than read. Every one needs human review.

unanswered.description: Questions the notes did not answer.

bullet.description: A bullet, optionally with a bold lead-in label and nested children.
